Overview
System Architecture

A single three-port DC-DC converter replaces three separate converters, reducing component count and enabling inter-port power sharing for a full EV powertrain.

Source

100 V Li-ion

50 Ah • 5 kWh • 100% SOC

Aggregate Rating

~9.1 kW

Three ports combined

Soft-Start

0.7 Ω Pre-charge

Surge bounded to ~143 A

Solver

Discrete 1 µs

Powergui • 20 s simulation

Traction Speed

1600 RPM

20 Nm rated • 10% torque ripple

Control

Field-Oriented (FOC)

Clarke • Park • Cascaded PI
PORT 1

Vehicle Traction Drive

  • Output: 230 V, 15–30 A
  • Load: PMSM (Rs=0.01Ω, Ld=Lq=3mH)
  • Flux linkage: 0.175 V·s, 4 pole pairs
  • Control: FOC • Speed PI + d-q current PI
  • Inverter LC filter: 10 µH / 100 µF, ESR 0.5Ω
  • Output filter: 5 mH / 470 µF
PORT 2

AC Compressor Drive

  • Output: 115 V, 8 A
  • Load: PMSM (Rs=0.718Ω, Ls=1.5mH)
  • Flux linkage: 0.082 V·s, 2 pole pairs
  • Load torque: 0–8 Nm variable profile
  • Output filter: 3 mH / 220 µF
PORT 3

Auxiliary Battery Charger

  • Output: 13 V, 101 A
  • Battery: 11 V, 34 Ah Li-ion, 20% SOC
  • Supplies: Infotainment, chassis, auxiliaries
  • Charge path: Series inductor + diode
  • Output filter: 0.5 mH / 47 µF

Control Strategy
Field-Oriented Control (FOC)

FOC decouples flux and torque in the rotating d-q reference frame, allowing the PMSM to be controlled like a DC machine using simple PI regulators.

AdvantageWhy it matters for this project
Independent torque & flux controlid=0 gives maximum torque per ampere for the traction PMSM
Fast torque responseCritical for the 10–25 Nm dynamic load profile
Low torque ripple10% ripple measured (2 Nm peak-to-peak at 20 Nm rated)
High efficiencyMinimum stator current for required torque
Simple PI regulatorsDC quantities in d-q frame, easy to tune and verify
Current limitingiq and id can be clamped directly
Simulation Results
Waveforms & Performance

All results from MATLAB/Simulink, 20 s discrete simulation at 1 µs sample time.

1

Converter Output Voltage Waveform

Three-port output voltages. Ports settle after the soft-start transient.

2

Converter Output Current Waveform

Output currents for all three ports over the full simulation.

3

Source Battery — Voltage, Current, SOC

100 V Li-ion source: voltage sags from ~100 V to ~85 V under full load. SOC declines from 100% to ~99.82% over 10 s.

4

Auxiliary Battery — Voltage, Current, SOC

11 V, 34 Ah Li-ion auxiliary battery charging from 20% SOC via Port 3 at 13 V.

5

AC Compressor PMSM — Speed & Torque

Speed response (top) and electromagnetic torque (bottom) for the compressor motor under a 0–8 Nm dynamic load profile.

6

Inverter Output Voltage — Port 2

Three-phase six-step inverter output voltage waveforms driving the AC compressor PMSM from the 115 V Port 2 bus.

7

Traction PMSM — Speed & Torque

FOC speed reference: 1600 RPM. Torque ripple: 10% (2 Nm peak-to-peak at 20 Nm rated). Dynamic load profile: 10–25 Nm.

8

Inverter Output Voltage — Port 1

Three-phase PWM inverter output voltage before the LC filter, feeding the traction PMSM from the 230 V Port 1 bus.

9

Port 1 Inverter Output After LC Filtering

Filtered sinusoidal phase voltages after the 10 µH / 100 µF output LC filter (ESR 0.5 Ω). Switching ripple significantly attenuated.

10

Input Current and Voltage

Source-side input current and voltage at the converter input. Soft-start inrush bounded by the 0.7 Ω pre-charge resistor (~143 A limit).
